title: Harnessing the skyrmion Hall effect for low-power skyrmion transport in a tubular synthetic antiferromagnet
authors: Ivan P. Miranda, Grzegorz J. Kwiatkowski, Jacob J. Mankenberg, Cecilia M. Holmqvist, Igor S. Lobanov, Valery M. Uzdin, Pavel F. Bessarab
abstract: We show that optimal control can turn the skyrmion Hall effect from a source of typically unwanted transverse motion into a mechanism for reducing Ohmic losses in skyrmion transport. We consider a pair of antiferromagnetically coupled skyrmions confined to a tubular geometry, where their relative transverse displacement becomes a periodic internal coordinate. The skyrmion Hall effect drives this coordinate, while finite interlayer coupling makes the resulting relation between applied current and longitudinal velocity nonlinear, allowing different current protocols to produce the same prescribed average velocity. We determine which of these protocols minimizes Joule heating. Depending on the interlayer coupling and spin-transfer-torque parameters, the optimal current is either constant, with the skyrmion pair maintaining a fixed relative position, or time dependent, with the pair undergoing periodic relative motion around the tube. In either case, the additional internal degree of freedom created by the skyrmion Hall effect and interlayer coupling enables skyrmion transport at a lower power than in the uncoupled limit.
summary: This work shows that in a tubular synthetic antiferromagnet, the skyrmion Hall effect can be harnessed using optimal control to minimize energy dissipation during transport. By treating the relative separation of the skyrmion pair as a controllable internal coordinate, the system can achieve lower power consumption than previously thought possible. This provides a mechanism to engineer energy-efficient spintronic devices.
main_problem: To demonstrate that the skyrmion Hall effect, usually a source of unwanted transverse motion, can be optimally controlled to reduce Ohmic losses during skyrmion transport.
main_result: By exploiting the internal separation mode created by the skyrmion Hall effect and interlayer coupling, the system can achieve low-power transport through either constant or time-dependent current protocols, outperforming the uncoupled limit.
method: Optimal control theory is applied to minimize the Joule heating power required to maintain a prescribed average skyrmion pair drift velocity.
model_or_system: The system models a pair of skyrmions confined to a tubular geometry within a synthetic antiferromagnet, governed by an atomistic spin Hamiltonian and dynamics derived from the Landau-Lifshitz equation.
key_observables: Average pair drift velocity (v_x), Ohmic power dissipation (P), and the power ratio P_dc/P_opt.
important_parameters: Interlayer coupling (J_perp), DMI magnitude (D_parallel), anisotropy (K_parallel), and STT parameters (zeta).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Adiabatic Approximation (AA), assuming dynamics follow slow, soft modes, and comparing results against the Rigid Approximation (RA).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the locked-to-winding boundary in parameter space and compare the power ratio P_dc/P_opt between optimal control and DC driving protocols.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the reduced two-coordinate model, then applies optimal control theory to minimize power for a target velocity, comparing the results across locked and winding dynamic regimes.
why_interesting: The use of optimal control theory to manipulate internal degrees of freedom (the separation mode) to suppress dissipation is a powerful concept applicable to open quantum systems where dissipation must be managed for coherent operation.
